contains.app: 1.8.66: Budget uses the phone journal design at every width. The legacy three-column Home and the Budget calendar, plan, timeline, and board view frames are removed; a single centered journal column (390–520 pt) is the only Budget presentation. The cash/owned a11y walker accepts the grouped read-only rows shape. Compared on Mac Chrome (Metal) at 1000×712 and 390×844 [MEAS]. 1.8.65: Budget phone art fidelity, all screens. Home Today/Plan/links match the study stack; calendar marks sit centered under the numerals; ledger captions, the date-picker month title, schedule wrapping, and the resilience legend/selected-day are tightened. Remaining study states (cash entry, plan alternatives B/C, add-item A/B/C, add-alternative A/B/C with the preferred star, day-item path, plan-switch review, debt, pay, and the schedule editor) are opened through the same act strings as Home. Compared on Mac Metal against the phone studies [MEAS]. 1.8.64: Budget phone art fidelity. Journal tokens match the approved phone studies: Source Sans 3, ink #24232B / #4D4C57 / #5C5B66, rules #DCDCE3 / #ECECF1, wash #ECEAF3, accent #7D74A8, mint #DDF0E6 / #1E5640, calendar tints #DDF0E6 / #F3EFD8 / #F3E6E8 with open-circle and bar marks, 44/48/56 pt rows, 28 pt group gaps, drawn chevrons. 1.8.63: Budget Home boot fix. The typography constant for 44 pt targets is now tapSz, so it no longer overwrites the hit() function (Safari: 'hit is not a function', 'hit' is 44). 1.8.62: phone-first journal layout (portrait 390, body 17 pt, 44 pt targets). Home schedule rows open the actions page. The mini month is the only month calendar. Every item is added through the calendar; there is no first-visit setup and no undated group in monthly expenses. Cash and owned items are added from a calendar day (that day is the as-of date) and default to Cash, with no name inference; the cash/owned list and monthly expenses are read-only. The shared date picker is an inline expansion. A missing data repo is created privately and automatically; an existing repo this key can use is reused, public or private. Sources and tests are delivered as a sidecar archive outside this repository. 1.8.61: audit repairs. Home's 'Scheduled this month' shows pay less costs instead of adding pay to costs; 'Schedule paydays' opens the Calendar with the pay form; 'Enter debts' stays until pay is scheduled; the synced budget is compressed before it is sealed and is sent after 10 quiet seconds instead of after every edit. 1.8.60: a dedicated launcher (Budget only, or Demo only) opens straight into its app and the platform refuses every route to another app (picker, saved last app, app routes, mounts); Back steps inside Budget (day, month, Home) before it reaches the app picker, and never reaches it from a dedicated launcher. On Budget Home, an entry in the day schedule opens 'Record what happened' for that entry; the section itself still opens the full day. 1.8.59: Budget syncs by itself when GitHub is connected: the budget and unfinished proposals are sealed with a key kept on this device (no passphrase to type), 'Copy transfer code' moves that key to another device once, an older passphrase-sealed copy asks for its passphrase once and is never overwritten unread, offline changes stay local and sync later, and when two devices both changed the budget both versions are kept for the user to choose. 1.8.58: calendar day colours are resilience, worked out automatically: each day is tested against an unexpected cost, late pay and an unavailable item that something depends on, counting only cash before the next pay and alternatives that are viable that day; the day view says why. 1.8.57: an entry's first alternative asks for the category the choices share; each choice has its own requirements, in force only while it is in use; 'Preferred' is a mark that starts a proposal instead of changing the plan; a proposal lists the requirements still to resolve, shows the full sequence before and after, is saved apart from the plan, and changes nothing until it is accepted. 1.8.56: the Calendar day view lists every entry with Change and Record what happened; a repeating entry asks 'this occurrence only' or 'this and future occurrences'; recording shows a before-and-after plan comparison that can be closed without undoing the record. 1.8.55: starting finances (cash or owned assets, debts with a calculated payment schedule, pay with fixed or percent deductions), 'every X days' recurrence, and occurrence overrides in the evaluator. 1.8.54: Calendar Add item (a Plan step, an existing item or a new item, then its time; add on the selected days or span across them), a span charges on its last day, routine items (schedule-only), and day boxes ordered by time. 1.8.53: Budget calendar days are coloured by plan risk (CRITICAL / MODERATE / LOW) from the workbook's cash-criticality rule: lowest balance before the next payday under $500 / $1,500, or a $200+ one-off, the rent or a plan step starting that day / within 3 days; blocked plan steps move no money. 1.8.52: calendar days show each step as a box tinted by kind (spending, income, debt payment), side by side with a small gap, wrapping only at the cell edge, with text shrinking until all of it fits and an item count under the date. 1.8.51: an atlas can keep its own Plan (meta.planOwn): the Plan lists only the steps the atlas puts on it, and Calendar or Board items are no longer copied onto it. 1.8.50: atlas handoff (a category's own actual runs until its selected alternative starts), Board sections (sort by category with each section's money), and a plan line on Board rows and Plan steps. 1.8.49: the Plan's step column computes for every step (money, value, requirement) instead of 'not computed'. 1.8.48: the account menu can create the public data repo when it is missing; Register pre-fills a key with Contents and Administration write. 1.8.47: Budget data (encrypted) in the account menu saves Budget's atlas to your data repo sealed with a passphrase (AES-GCM, PBKDF2-SHA-256 600k) and loads it back; Budget's surplus and living cost count spending as spent. 1.8.46: Budget journal (Ash): a Budget Home (month, today, plan and the month's ledger) and journal presentations of the full Calendar, Plan and Expense/Income/Debt/Asset Boards, with one shared hover date picker; other apps keep the stock skin. 1.8.45: Safe area: the platform bar, app picker, menus and apps stay clear of notches, the home indicator and rounded window / screen corners (viewport-fit=cover, env(safe-area-inset-*), plus a corner allowance where devices report no inset). 1.8.44: Budget is the default app and comes first in the app picker; the Fish and Lumen overlay demo apps and their view packs are removed (the platform file is about 0.5 MB smaller). Exp7 stays as an app (lean demo and test harness). 1.8.43: Fixes from Ash's review of 1.8.42: a gradient hover colour no longer turns a skin's face transparent (hover re-emits the node); bold gradient text draws (rich runs turn a gradient colour into the item's paint); a scene placed twice with one placement clipped keeps separate remapped uniforms (images too); non-finite gradient values are rejected in JS; a name longer than its field shows its start with an ellipsis instead of spilling out; demo labels name the vector models. 1.8.42: Gradient paints (linear, two-circle radial, conic; pad / repeat / reflect; any number of stops) on any draw item, and stroked paths (width, miter / round / bevel joins with a miter limit, butt / round / square caps, dashes with an offset) in JRender's draw-list core; JRender.linear / radial / conic and stroke() in the builders, ['stroke', ...] items in JRViews, Exp7VM.linear / radial / conic / strokeItem for skins. Existing scenes tessellate byte-identically. 1.8.41: Renderer fixes from Ash's review: the image layer draws through the renderer's overlay hook instead of replacing draw(), so budgeted off-screen work keeps running; a scene reaching past the canvas gets a valid full-canvas viewport with an exact uniform remap; images use the full-canvas viewport their shader expects. 1.8.40: JRender's wasm is the same dl-index build run through wasm-opt (289,561 B -> 256,009 B); no behaviour change. 1.8.39: Calendar, Board and Plan are vector view models built from the atlas (Exp7VM), with view options, a default skin and per-app tokens; the HTML view builders and the HTML layout path for these views are removed. 1.8.38: the Calendar selection counter follows the selection (it stayed at "0 day(s) selected"). 1.8.37: JRender with an indexed draw-list core (scroll, patch, hover and load no longer walk the whole scene; growth uploads only changed vertices) and a 4 ms frame budget for off-screen tessellation, so on-screen rows are drawn live and the margin catches up. 1.8.36: The parallax holds still while a view scrolls and resumes 160 ms after the last scroll, with no jump; edges redraw only when their drawn offset changes, and frames with nothing to change send no patch and draw nothing extra. 1.8.35: Board scrolling and layout scale with what is on screen: parallax moves only slabs within a screen of the viewport, in 1/8 px steps, and the state-layer layout pass (roomBelow, ground-shadow ids) is linear instead of quadratic, with identical layout output. Board category-name fields are created only for rows near the viewport and added as you scroll. 1.8.34: The old ranking code is gone: no Exp6 JGroup.Best()/SimulatedBest() ranking, fallback or inline kernel copies; JAtlasModel.exp6Order is now rankAlts and JFEngine (Exp7Rank) is the only ranking path. Picks, orders and scores are unchanged. 1.8.33: Exp7 ranks alternatives with JFEngine (Lore jeditor r29) instead of Exp6 JGroup.Best()/SimulatedBest(): each group scores as one batch (jfactor terms through the Exp6 kernel via JFEngine) and ranks by score, highest first, ties in list order, giving the same order as Best() on every shipped group. jfactor() now uses the real Exp6 kernel (method 2). 1.8.32: The Path inspector on the Atlas, Proposal console and Two writers tabs lists the paths the last proposal touched plus a 20-path preview; the full match list is built only while you search it (up to 200), and the Paths tab still lists everything. Opening those tabs no longer lays out all 1,192 rows. 1.8.31: Board values show as the value with its unit, red when consuming and green when not. An item's other buttons sit on a line under it, and item lists start hidden. The Budget date is one button that opens a mini calendar over the view. Board rows move with the pointer again.
